summary: Famous whistleblower cases and the long timeline, mostly from primary documents: DOJ, SEC, CFTC, NHTSA and DOL press releases (justice.gov copies via Wayback raw captures because the live site serves a bot check), US public laws from GovInfo, the SEC inspector general's Madoff report, an ECHR Grand Chamber judgment, a Swiss Federal Supreme Court decision and the 2026 Eleventh Circuit Zafirov opinion. Press is used only where agencies are silent (Birkenfeld's IRS award, the Libor link to the CFTC record award, the GSK 2012 relator share, Wilkinson, Falciani, names of whistleblowers). Case amounts are written as plain numbers because cases.csv has no scale column; each row's notes give the amount as printed.

cases.summary: UBS, Switzerland's largest bank, entered a deferred prosecution agreement for helping US clients hide accounts from the IRS, agreed to hand over client names and to pay $780 million. The release also notes that former UBS banker Bradley Birkenfeld had pleaded guilty in June 2008.
cases.quote: As part of the deferred prosecution agreement, UBS has further agreed to pay $780 million in fines, penalties, interest and restitution.
cases.notes: Printed as '$780 million'. DOJ does not call Birkenfeld a whistleblower in this release; his information is credited in the IRS award (see AP row). Not itself a whistleblower award; listed as the case behind the IRS's largest award.

cases.summary: The IRS paid former UBS banker Bradley Birkenfeld $104 million for information on US tax evasion at UBS, then the largest IRS award. He had himself served about two and a half years in prison for conspiracy in the same matter. The IRS confirmed the award because he signed a disclosure waiver.
cases.quote: The U.S. tax agency has awarded a former Swiss banker $104 million for providing information about overseas tax cheats — the largest amount ever awarded by the Internal Revenue Service
cases.notes: Amounts as printed: '$104 million' award; '$780 million fine' against UBS. Reported by AP, announced by his lawyers; the IRS does not publish award orders. Prison: DOJ release of 2009-08-21 (40 months, see events).

cases.target: 80 Swiss banks (DOJ Swiss Bank Program, Category 2)
cases.summary: Follow-on to the UBS case: under the Swiss Bank Program announced in August 2013, DOJ signed non-prosecution agreements with 80 Swiss banks and imposed more than $1.36 billion in penalties; the last Category 2 agreement (HSZH Verwaltungs AG) was announced on this date.
cases.quote: The department has executed agreements with 80 banks since March 30, 2015, when it announced the first Swiss Bank Program non-prosecution agreement with BSI SA.  The department has imposed a total of more than $1.36 billion in Swiss Bank penalties
cases.notes: Printed as 'more than $1.36 billion'. Not a whistleblower award; context for the UBS/Birkenfeld case. The DOJ programme page later lists further agreements and addenda up to 2020 (raw/usa-doj-swiss-bank-program-page-2025.html).

cases.summary: Danske Bank pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit bank fraud over non-resident customers of its Estonian branch and agreed to forfeit $2.059 billion; DOJ credited about $850 million paid to the SEC and Danish authorities. DOJ says the bank knew of the problems by 2014 partly from 'an internal whistleblower'.
cases.location: paragraph beginning 'Today, Danske Bank pleaded guilty'
cases.quote: Under the terms of the plea agreement, the company has agreed to criminal forfeiture of $2.059 billion.
cases.notes: Printed as '$2.059 billion'. DOJ does not name the whistleblower; Howard Wilkinson went public himself (see WNN row). Same release: SEC settlement 'approximately $413 million' including a $178.6 million civil penalty.

cases.summary: Howard Wilkinson, former head of Danske Bank's Baltic trading unit, reported the Estonian branch's laundering internally in 2013-2014 and later went public. As of February 2023 no US whistleblower award had been paid in the case.
cases.quote: While no whistleblower award has been paid in connection with the case, it is public knowledge that the scheme was uncovered by Wilkinson’s whistleblowing.
cases.notes: Sanctions amount is the SEC civil penalty placed in a Fair Fund ('$178.6 million'). Outlet is linked to Wilkinson's lawyers; no later official statement on an award found. program_id usa-sec-wb only because the article discusses the SEC programme; no award claim is documented.

cases.summary: The CFTC paid its largest award, nearly $200 million, to one whistleblower whose information significantly contributed to an open investigation and two related actions by a US federal regulator and a foreign regulator. The CFTC does not name the case (award order 21-WB-07).
cases.quote: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced an award of nearly $200 million to a whistleblower
cases.notes: Printed as 'nearly $200 million'; the CFTC withholds the exact amount and the case name. Press reports link it to Deutsche Bank's Libor settlement (see City A.M. row). Order number 21-WB-07.

cases.summary: Press reports, citing unnamed sources, identified the CFTC's record award as going to a former Deutsche Bank employee who raised the alarm about Libor rigging, tied to the bank's 2015 US settlement.
cases.quote: sources familiar with the matter have identified them as a former Deutsche Bank employee, and the payout is understood to be related to the £2.5bn settlement the bank paid to US authorities in 2015.
cases.notes: Award printed as 'almost $200m'. Identification not confirmed by the CFTC. Note the article's '£2.5bn' (DOJ/CFTC/NYDFS/FCA total is usually given in US dollars).

cases.summary: The CFTC fined Deutsche Bank $800 million for manipulating and falsely reporting LIBOR and Euribor from at least 2005 to early 2011, then the largest fine in CFTC history; the CFTC said it had imposed over $4 billion in penalties on 13 banks and brokers for LIBOR and FX benchmark abuses.
cases.quote: This Order requires Deutsche Bank to pay a civil monetary penalty of $800 million
cases.notes: Printed as '$800 million'. The enforcement action reported to underlie the 2021 record CFTC award (not confirmed by the CFTC).

cases.summary: GSK pleaded guilty and paid $3 billion ($1 billion criminal, $2 billion civil) over off-label promotion of Paxil and Wellbutrin, Avandia safety data and price reporting, then the largest health care fraud settlement in US history. The off-label part resolved four qui tam suits.
cases.location: para 1; off-label section (paragraph after the $1.043 billion figure)
cases.quote: This off-label civil settlement resolves four lawsuits pending in federal court in the District of Massachusetts under the qui tam, or whistleblower, provisions of the False Claims Act
cases.notes: Printed as '$3 billion'. The DOJ release does not state the relators' share; see Management Today row.

cases.whistleblower: Blair Hamrick; Thomas Gerahty; Matthew Burke; Greg Thorpe
cases.summary: Four former GSK employees were reported to share about $250 million from the 2012 settlement as qui tam relators.
cases.quote: That's how much money four employees will share after giving evidence that helped US authorities build a case against GlaxoSmithKline's sales practices.
cases.notes: Award printed as '$250m' (headline and 'Stat of the day: $250m'). Secondary report; the names are as published by the magazine (the relators spoke publicly).

cases.target: Pfizer Inc. and Pharmacia & Upjohn Company Inc.
cases.summary: Pfizer paid $2.3 billion over illegal promotion of Bextra and other drugs, then DOJ's largest health care fraud settlement, including a $1 billion civil False Claims Act settlement triggered by qui tam suits. Six whistleblowers received more than $102 million from the federal share.
cases.quote: As a part of today’s resolution, six whistleblowers will receive payments totaling more than $102 million from the federal share of the civil recovery.
cases.notes: Printed as '$2.3 billion' and 'more than $102 million' (six relators combined). Names not given by DOJ.

cases.summary: GSK's subsidiary pleaded guilty over adulterated drugs from its Cidra, Puerto Rico plant; $150 million criminal fine and forfeiture plus a $600 million civil settlement. Whistleblower Cheryl Eckard, named by DOJ, received about $96 million.
cases.quote: As part of today’s resolution, the whistleblower - Cheryl Eckard - will receive approximately $96 million from the federal share of the settlement amount.
cases.notes: Printed as '$750 Million' (headline) and 'approximately $96 million'.

cases.target: Bernard L. Madoff Investment Securities (Bernard Madoff)
cases.summary: Harry Markopolos warned the SEC in May 2000, March 2001 and October 2005 ('The World's Largest Hedge Fund is a Fraud', about 30 red flags). The SEC's inspector general found the SEC never ran a competent investigation before Madoff confessed in December 2008. No reward: the SEC programme did not exist until 2010.
cases.quote: The complaint submitted in 2005 was entitled “The World’s Largest Hedge Fund is a Fraud” and detailed approximately 30 red flags indicating that Madoff was operating a Ponzi scheme
cases.notes: Markopolos is named throughout the OIG report. 'No reward' is a statement of context (the Dodd-Frank programme came in 2010); no award source exists.

cases.summary: OSHA ordered Wells Fargo to reinstate a Los Angeles-area branch manager fired in 2010 after reporting suspected bank, mail and wire fraud, and to pay back pay, damages and fees of about $5.4 million under Sarbanes-Oxley. This is retaliation relief, not a reward.
cases.quote: Back pay, compensatory damages, and attorneys’ fees were together calculated at about $5.4 million.
cases.notes: About $5.4 million ordered as damages to the whistleblower (not a reward, so left out of award_amount). OSHA does not name complainants. Wells Fargo could appeal; outcome of any appeal not checked.

cases.target: Wells Fargo & Company; Wells Fargo Bank, N.A.
cases.summary: Wells Fargo paid $3 billion (deferred prosecution agreement, FIRREA civil settlement and SEC proceedings) over 2002-2016 sales practices that opened millions of accounts without customer consent.
cases.quote: have agreed to pay $3 billion to resolve their potential criminal and civil liability stemming from a practice between 2002 and 2016
cases.notes: Printed as '$3 billion'. No whistleblower award linked to this resolution was found.

cases.summary: Boeing entered a deferred prosecution agreement on a charge of conspiracy to defraud the FAA over the 737 MAX (MCAS), paying over $2.5 billion: $243.6 million penalty, $1.77 billion to airline customers, $500 million fund for crash victims' heirs.
cases.quote: Boeing will pay a total criminal monetary amount of over $2.5 billion, composed of a criminal monetary penalty of $243.6 million, compensation payments to Boeing’s 737 MAX airline customers of $1.77 billion
cases.notes: Printed as 'over $2.5 billion'. No whistleblower reward applies (aviation whistleblowers have retaliation protection, not rewards).

cases.whistleblower: Sam Salehpour; Ed Pierson; Joe Jacobsen; John Barnett
cases.summary: A Senate subcommittee heard Boeing whistleblowers. The chair described harassment, isolation, transfers and threats against Sam Salehpour, thanked Ed Pierson and Joe Jacobsen, and noted that John Barnett, a former quality manager turned whistleblower, had died by suicide in March 2024.
cases.quote: These whistleblowers have come forward at great personal risk. In fact, a number of them and others have suffered harassment, isolation, transfers, and even threats of physical violence.
cases.notes: Names as given by the Senate chair; the statement spells Jacobsen both 'Jacobsen' and 'Jacobson'. No reward programme involved.

cases.summary: The SEC paid its largest award, nearly $279 million, to one whistleblower whose information and assistance led to SEC and related actions, more than double its previous record of $114 million (October 2020).
cases.quote: The Securities and Exchange Commission today announced the largest-ever award, nearly $279 million, to a whistleblower
cases.notes: Printed as 'nearly $279 million'. The SEC does not name the case.

cases.target: Hyundai Motor America; Kia Motors America
cases.summary: NHTSA's first whistleblower award: more than $24 million, the maximum percentage allowed by law of the $81 million collected, for information on Theta II engine recalls; the 2020 consent orders carried $210 million in combined penalties.
cases.quote: This award is the maximum percentage allowed by law of the $81 million in cash collected by the United States and is the first award NHTSA has issued under its authority.
cases.notes: Award printed as 'more than $24 million'. NHTSA does not name the whistleblower; Kim Gwang-ho went public (see CNN row).

cases.target: Hyundai Motor America; Kia Motors America
cases.summary: The NHTSA award went to former Hyundai engineer Kim Gwang-ho, who reported the Theta II engine problems to NHTSA in 2016 and issued his own statement on the award.
cases.quote: handing out more than $24 million to a former Hyundai employee who provided key information about safety lapses at the South Korean carmaker.
cases.notes: Printed as 'more than $24 million'. CNN calls it the biggest auto-sector whistleblower award globally 'according to law firm Constantine Cannon, which represented Kim' (interested source).

cases.summary: The Swiss Federal Criminal Court convicted former HSBC IT employee Hervé Falciani in his absence of aggravated economic espionage over the leaked client data ('HSBC files') and sentenced him to five years; he was acquitted of the other charges and lived in France, out of reach of extradition. No reward.
cases.quote: Das Bundesstrafgericht hat den früheren HSBC-Mitarbeiter Hervé Falciani wegen Wirtschaftsspionage zu einer Freiheitsstrafe von fünf Jahren verurteilt.
cases.notes: Contrast case: prosecuted, not rewarded. Court judgment itself (SK.2014.46) not retrieved.

cases.target: Bank Julius Bär & Co. AG / Julius Baer Bank & Trust Company Ltd. (Cayman Islands)
cases.summary: Rudolf Elmer, former chief accountant of Julius Bär's Cayman Islands subsidiary, was prosecuted in Zurich for leaking client data to tax authorities, media and WikiLeaks. Zurich courts convicted him in 2011 and 2015 (suspended day-fines); in 2016 the Zurich High Court acquitted him of bank-secrecy offences but gave him a suspended 14-month sentence for threats and forgery, with 220 days already served in pre-trial detention. The Federal Supreme Court upheld the bank-secrecy acquittal in 2018. No reward.
cases.quote: fällte sie eine Freiheitsstrafe von 14 Monaten, wovon 220 Tage durch Untersuchungshaft erstanden seien.
cases.notes: The judgment is anonymised ('X.'); Elmer went public himself and is named for this ruling by law.ch (che-lawch-elmer-2018). Earlier sentences in the same judgment: 240 day-fines of CHF 30 (2011) and 300 day-fines of CHF 150 (2015), both suspended.

cases.summary: LuxLeaks: Raphaël Halet, a former PwC employee who passed tax returns to a journalist, was convicted in Luxembourg (fine of EUR 1,000 after appeal). The ECHR Grand Chamber held 12 votes to 5 that the conviction violated freedom of expression and awarded him EUR 15,000 for non-pecuniary damage and EUR 40,000 in costs. No reward.
cases.quote: Holds, by twelve votes to five, that there has been a violation of Article 10
cases.notes: Damages, not a reward. Halet is named in the judgment.

cases.summary: LuxLeaks: Antoine Deltour, the former PwC auditor who took the tax rulings, was convicted in 2016 (12-month suspended sentence and EUR 1,500 fine). On 11 January 2018 Luxembourg's Court of Cassation quashed his conviction on whistleblower grounds, and in May 2018 the Court of Appeal acquitted him of the offences linked to the documents given to the journalist. He was never before the ECHR: the 2023 Grand Chamber case was Halet's. No reward.
cases.quote: A.D. was sentenced to a twelve-month prison term, suspended in its entirety, and to a fine of EUR 1,500.
cases.notes: The judgment calls him 'A.D.'; he went public himself and is named by Paperjam (lux-paperjam-halet-2023: 'Deltour was then recognised as a whistleblower by the Court of Cassation'). Correction to the brief: the 2023 ECHR acquittal-type ruling concerned Halet, not Deltour. A remaining conviction over internal training documents ended with the sentence suspended (para 48).

cases.target: Florida Medical Associates, LLC (VipCare) and related entities
cases.summary: Dr Clarissa Zafirov's 2019 qui tam suit alleged false Medicare diagnosis codes. In 2024 the district court dismissed it, holding qui tam relators are unappointed officers in breach of the Appointments Clause. On 1 September 2026 the Eleventh Circuit vacated that ruling and remanded for the remaining constitutional arguments.
cases.quote: we vacate the district court’s order dismissing this case and remand for the district court to evaluate the defendants’ remaining constitutional arguments.
cases.notes: Case remains pending on Take Care and Vesting Clause arguments.

events.title: False Claims Act enacted ('Lincoln Law')
events.description: Congress passed the False Claims Act during the Civil War against fraud by defence contractors; it lets private citizens sue on the government's behalf (qui tam) and share in the recovery.
events.quote: a federal statute originally enacted in 1863 in response to defense contractor fraud during the American Civil War

events.title: False Claims Amendments Act of 1986
events.description: The 1986 amendments revived qui tam suits: a relator gets 15-25% of the proceeds when the government takes over the case and 25-30% when the relator goes it alone.
events.quote: receive at least 15 percent but not more than 25 percent of the proceeds of the action or settlement of the claim

events.title: Sarbanes-Oxley Act section 806: protection for corporate whistleblowers
events.description: Section 806 created a civil action against retaliation for employees of listed companies who report fraud (18 U.S.C. 1514A). Protection only, no reward.
events.quote: PROTECTION FOR EMPLOYEES OF PUBLICLY TRADED COMPANIES WHO PROVIDE EVIDENCE OF FRAUD.

events.title: Tax Relief and Health Care Act of 2006: mandatory IRS whistleblower awards
events.description: Section 406 made IRS awards mandatory at 15-30% of collected proceeds for large cases (over $2 million in dispute; individuals with gross income over $200,000) and created the Whistleblower Office.
events.quote: receive as an award at least 15 percent but not more than 30 percent of the collected proceeds

events.title: Birkenfeld pleads guilty
events.description: Former UBS private banker Bradley Birkenfeld pleaded guilty to conspiring to defraud the United States.
events.quote: On June 19, 2008, Birkenfeld pleaded guilty to conspiring to defraud the United States

events.title: UBS deferred prosecution agreement: $780 million and client names
events.description: UBS admitted helping US taxpayers hide accounts, agreed to give the US client identities and to pay $780 million.
events.quote: Agrees to Identify Customers & Pay $780 Million

events.title: Birkenfeld sentenced to 40 months
events.description: Bradley Birkenfeld was sentenced to 40 months in prison, despite having given the government information on UBS. (Two days earlier UBS agreed to disclose 4,450 more accounts.)
events.quote: has been sentenced to 40 months incarceration by Judge William J. Zloch in Fort Lauderdale, Fla.

events.title: SEC inspector general: Madoff warnings ignored
events.description: The SEC OIG found that between 1992 and 2008 the SEC received six substantive complaints about Madoff, including Harry Markopolos's, but never ran a competent investigation.
events.quote: the SEC received six 10 substantive complaints that raised significant red flags concerning Madoff’s hedge fund operations

events.title: Pfizer $2.3 billion settlement, then the largest health care fraud settlement
events.description: Pfizer paid $2.3 billion; six whistleblowers received more than $102 million.
events.quote: have agreed to pay $2.3 billion, the largest health care fraud settlement in the history of the Department of Justice

events.title: Dodd-Frank Act creates SEC and CFTC whistleblower award programmes
events.description: Sections 922 (SEC) and 748 (CFTC) require awards of 10-30% of monetary sanctions collected in successful actions.
events.quote: not less than 10 percent, in total, of what has been collected of the monetary sanctions imposed in the action or related actions

events.title: Dodd-Frank Act section 748: CFTC whistleblower programme
events.description: Section 748 added commodity whistleblower incentives and protection to the Commodity Exchange Act.
events.quote: SEC. 748. COMMODITY WHISTLEBLOWER INCENTIVES AND PROTECTION.

events.title: GSK/SB Pharmco $750 million; whistleblower Cheryl Eckard gets about $96 million
events.description: Named relator Cheryl Eckard received about $96 million from the federal share.
events.quote: the whistleblower - Cheryl Eckard - will receive approximately $96 million

events.title: GSK $3 billion, largest health care fraud settlement in US history
events.description: GSK pleaded guilty and paid $3 billion; four qui tam suits resolved.
events.quote: The resolution is the largest health care fraud settlement in U.S. history and the largest payment ever by a drug company.

events.title: IRS pays Birkenfeld $104 million
events.description: Largest IRS whistleblower award to date, paid to a whistleblower who had served prison time in the same affair.
events.quote: the largest amount ever awarded by the Internal Revenue Service, lawyers for the whistleblower announced Tuesday

events.title: DOJ announces the Swiss Bank Program
events.description: A path for Swiss banks to resolve US tax-evasion liability by disclosure, cooperation and penalties; a consequence of the UBS case.
events.quote: The Swiss Bank Program, which was announced on Aug. 29, 2013, provides a path for Swiss banks to resolve potential criminal liabilities in the United States.

events.title: CFTC fines Deutsche Bank $800 million for Libor manipulation
events.description: Largest CFTC fine at the time; CFTC total for LIBOR and FX abuses passed $4 billion across 13 banks and brokers.
events.quote: With Today’s Action, the CFTC Has Imposed over $4 Billion in Penalties against 13 Banks and Brokers to Address LIBOR and FX Benchmark Abuses

events.title: Falciani sentenced in absentia to five years
events.description: Switzerland's Federal Criminal Court convicted the HSBC leaker of economic espionage.
events.quote: Das Gericht befand Falciani des wirtschaftlichen Nachrichtendienstes schuldig.

events.title: Swiss Bank Program: final Category 2 agreement, 80 banks, over $1.36 billion
events.description: DOJ's last Category 2 non-prosecution agreement under the Swiss Bank Program.
events.quote: Department’s Swiss Bank Program Imposed More Than $1.3 Billion in Penalties on 80 Banks

events.title: LuxLeaks: Deltour and Halet convicted at first instance
events.description: Luxembourg District Court convicted A.D. (Antoine Deltour) and Raphaël Halet, among others of theft from an employer and breach of professional secrecy.
events.quote: On 29 June 2016 the Luxembourg District Court, sitting as a criminal court, convicted A.D. and the applicant

events.title: OSHA orders Wells Fargo to reinstate whistleblower
events.description: Sarbanes-Oxley retaliation order worth about $5.4 million.
events.quote: has ordered Wells Fargo Bank N.A. to compensate and immediately reinstate a former bank manager

events.title: LuxLeaks: Court of Cassation recognises Deltour as a whistleblower
events.description: The Court of Cassation quashed A.D.'s (Deltour's) conviction, holding that whistleblower status must cover all offences linked to the disclosure; Halet's appeal was dismissed the same day.
events.quote: quashed the Court of Appeal’s judgment on the grounds that whistle-blower status ought in principle to be recognised

events.title: Swiss Federal Supreme Court upholds Elmer's bank-secrecy acquittal
events.description: The court held Elmer, employed by a Cayman Islands subsidiary, was not bound by Swiss banking secrecy.
events.quote: Das Bundesgericht gab soeben bekannt gegeben, dass es den Freispruch von Rudolf Elmer vom Vorwurf der mehrfachen Verletzung des Bankgeheimnisses bestätigt habe.

events.title: EU Whistleblowing Directive (2019/1937) adopted
events.description: EU-wide minimum protection for people who report breaches of EU law; protection only, no rewards. Member States had to transpose it by 17 December 2021.
events.quote: Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 17 December 2021.

events.title: Wells Fargo pays $3 billion over fake accounts
events.description: DOJ/SEC resolution of the sales-practices scandal.
events.quote: Wells Fargo Agrees to Pay $3 Billion to Resolve Criminal and Civil Investigations into Sales Practices

events.title: Anti-Money Laundering Act of 2020 (NDAA FY2021, section 6314) updates AML whistleblower awards
events.description: Section 6314 rewrote 31 U.S.C. 5323: awards of up to 30% of sanctions collected in Bank Secrecy Act actions over $1 million.
events.quote: in an aggregate amount equal to not more than 30 percent, in total, of what has been collected of the monetary sanctions imposed in the action or related actions

events.title: Boeing 737 MAX deferred prosecution agreement, over $2.5 billion
events.description: Boeing charged with conspiracy to defraud the FAA.
events.quote: Boeing Charged with 737 Max Fraud Conspiracy and Agrees to Pay over $2.5 Billion

events.title: CFTC record award of nearly $200 million
events.description: Largest award to a single whistleblower at the time; press reports tie it to Deutsche Bank's Libor case.
events.quote: Largest Award to a Single Whistleblower

events.title: NHTSA's first whistleblower award: more than $24 million (Hyundai/Kia)
events.description: First award under NHTSA's vehicle-safety whistleblower authority.
events.quote: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration today announced it is making its first ever whistleblower award.

events.title: Danske Bank pleads guilty; $2 billion forfeiture
events.description: Resolution of the Estonian branch laundering case exposed by Howard Wilkinson.
events.quote: Largest Bank in Denmark Agrees to Forfeit $2 Billion

events.title: ECHR Grand Chamber: Halet v. Luxembourg
events.description: LuxLeaks whistleblower Raphaël Halet's conviction violated Article 10 (freedom of expression); EUR 15,000 damages plus EUR 40,000 costs.
events.quote: Holds, by twelve votes to five, that there has been a violation of Article 10

events.title: SEC record award of nearly $279 million
events.description: Largest SEC whistleblower award, more than double the October 2020 record of $114 million.
events.quote: more than doubling the $114 million whistleblower award the SEC issued in October 2020

events.title: Senate hearing with Boeing whistleblowers
events.description: The Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations heard Sam Salehpour and others on Boeing's safety culture and retaliation.
events.quote: Our purpose today is to hear from whistleblowers who have personal, eyewitness, factual stories to tell about Boeing

events.title: DOJ Corporate Whistleblower Awards Pilot Program begins
events.description: Three-year DOJ Criminal Division pilot paying discretionary awards from forfeitures over $1 million: up to 30% of the first $100 million net forfeited, up to 5% from $100-500 million.
events.quote: has been effective since August 1, 2024

events.title: Zafirov: district court holds FCA qui tam provisions unconstitutional
events.description: The Middle District of Florida held that relators are officers who must be appointed under Article II and dismissed Dr Zafirov's qui tam suit (751 F. Supp. 3d 1293).

events.title: DOJ pilot expanded to four more priority areas
events.description: After the Criminal Division memo of 12 May 2025, the pilot added areas such as trade, tariff and customs fraud, immigration violations, sanctions and cartels.
events.quote: In May 2025, the CWA expanded to cover four additional priority areas of focus.

events.title: Eleventh Circuit upholds qui tam under the Appointments Clause (Zafirov)
events.description: The appeals court vacated the 2024 dismissal, joining other circuits, and remanded for the remaining Take Care and Vesting Clause arguments.
events.quote: we join our sister circuits that have addressed this issue and hold that the qui tam provisions of the FCA do not violate the Appointments Clause.

programs.name: Corporate Whistleblower Awards Pilot Program (DOJ Criminal Division)
programs.notes: Three-year pilot; discretionary awards from criminal or civil forfeitures over $1 million. Id guessed from the raw file names another pass used (usa-doj-cwap-*); align with that pass if it chose a different program_id.

gaps: Birkenfeld's IRS award: no IRS document. The IRS does not publish award decisions; the $104 million figure comes from AP (his lawyers announced it, and the IRS confirmed it under his waiver). The exact release date from prison is not in an official source either; AP says he served 'about two-and-a-half years'.

GSK 2012: DOJ's release does not give the relators' share; only the press figure ($250m, Management Today) is recorded. The USAO Massachusetts release and the relator settlement agreements were not retrieved.
Pfizer 2009: DOJ gives only the combined 'more than $102 million' for six relators, without names or split.

Libor/Forex: the CFTC never names the case behind an award. The Deutsche Bank link to the 2021 record award rests on unnamed sources (City A.M.). No Forex-linked CFTC award could be tied to a case from a primary source.

Danske Bank / Howard Wilkinson: no official statement on any US award claim. Only an advocacy-linked outlet (Feb 2023) saying no award had been paid; Wilkinson's European Parliament (TAX3) testimony of Nov 2018 was not retrieved.

Wells Fargo: no whistleblower award is linked to the 2020 $3 billion resolution. Only the 2017 OSHA retaliation order (about $5.4 million, anonymous) is recorded; whether the order survived appeal was not checked.

Boeing: no reward programme applies. FAA/OSHA AIR21 retaliation decisions (e.g. for John Barnett) and the 2024-2025 plea/non-prosecution proceedings in the Northern District of Texas were not retrieved.
Falciani: the Swiss Federal Criminal Court judgment (SK.2014.46, 27 Nov 2015) and Spain's 2013 and 2018 refusals to extradite him were not retrieved; only SRF's report is used.
Elmer: the Federal Supreme Court press release of 10 Oct 2018 was not found on bger.ch (the decision BGE 145 IV 114 is stored instead).

Brief correction: Antoine Deltour was not acquitted by the ECHR in 2023. Luxembourg's Court of Cassation quashed his conviction on 11 Jan 2018 and the Court of Appeal acquitted him in May 2018. The 2023 ECHR Grand Chamber ruling (Halet v. Luxembourg) concerned his co-defendant Raphaël Halet.
1863 False Claims Act: the original Act of March 2, 1863 (12 Stat. 696) was not stored; the event cites DOJ's description. The month and day are therefore not given.
Zafirov district court ruling (751 F. Supp. 3d 1293, M.D. Fla. 2024): the order itself was not retrieved; the date is given as 2024 from the Eleventh Circuit's citation.

Not covered: AML Whistleblower Improvement Act of December 2022 (sanctions-evasion awards), the 2015 FAST Act motor-vehicle whistleblower law, Polansky v. Executive Health Resources (2023) and Digital Realty v. Somers (2018). The Supreme Court PDF URLs tried returned 404.
Record awards: the SEC record award ($279 million, 2023) and the CFTC record ($200 million, 2021) are recorded as of their dates; later records, if any, are left to the SEC/CFTC passes.
leads: Halet v. Luxembourg, Chamber judgment of 11 May 2021 (HUDOC 001-210131), for the earlier ECHR loss: https://hudoc.echr.coe.int/eng?i=001-210131
DOJ Swiss Bank Program press releases for each NPA (linked from raw/usa-doj-swiss-bank-program-page-2025.html), for per-bank penalties.
USAO Massachusetts release on GSK (July 2012) for the relators' share: search justice.gov/usao-ma archives.
European Parliament TAX3 committee hearing with Howard Wilkinson, 21 Nov 2018 (europarl.europa.eu).
SEC OIG Report OIG-509 Exhibit 1 (Markopolos testimony) and House Financial Services hearing of 4 Feb 2009 (GovInfo CHRG-111hhrg48291) for Markopolos's own account.
